fr:title.text: Website publishing — paths forward without a fork

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Website publishing — paths forward without a fork

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Planning tree for Website Publishing Redesign. Captures the constraint change since that TODO was written and lays out concrete paths forward.

New constraint. We no longer maintain a fork of forester. ~/ocaml-forester is now on upstream main. All publishing must be expressible in upstream 5.0; whatever filtering scheme we pick has to either (a) live inside what upstream already supports or (b) be implemented as a wrapper around the build, not as a compiler patch.

What upstream 5.0 actually offers for selective publishing. Effectively nothing tag-aware. Config.t in lib/core/Config.ml is just a record with fields trees, assets, foreign, url, home. The only built-in lever for "what gets published" is the [forest] trees = [...] array — i.e. which on-disk directories the build ingests. There is no [publish] section, no exclude_tags, no exclude_queries. (Those existed in the fork and were what the old public.toml flow leaned on conceptually, even though it just narrowed trees to trees/public/.)
Consequence. Any "publish all of trees/ except tagged X" semantics has to be synthesized outside forester. The compiler will not help us drop a tree from output based on its tags.

html:ul.html:li: A. Two-directory split (restore the old shape). Keep trees/public/ as the publishable surface. Add back a public.toml whose [forest] trees = ["trees/public"]. Build with that config and ship the output. Pros: zero leakage by construction; trivial to implement; matches upstream's only built-in lever; works today. Cons: keeps the hard public/private split that prompted the redesign — a private tree cannot transclude or link to a public one cleanly, and promoting a private tree to public means physically moving it.

B. Pre-build prune wrapper. Wrapper script that, before forester build, materializes a temp copy of trees/ with excluded trees physically removed (and broken transclusions either stubbed or stripped). Build runs against the pruned copy with [forest] trees = [<temp-dir>]. Pros: single source of truth in trees/; no compiler dependency; trees can move between "publishable" and "not" by tag, not by directory. Cons: implementation cost; broken-link / dangling-transclusion handling is the hard part; forester new, edit shortcuts, and the dev server keep working against the live trees/, so this only runs in the publish path.

C. Post-build scrub. Build the full forest, then walk the output tree and remove (or rewrite) HTML/XML for excluded URIs plus references to them. Pros: orthogonal to forester. Cons: fragile — has to understand the output layout, the manifest, and the XSL output simultaneously; easy to leave dangling pointers in transcluded content; harder than B for the same goal.

D. Custom manifest + selective copy. Build the full forest into an intermediate output/, then drive the published surface from a manifest of allowed tree IDs (built from a Datalog query over the full build's forest.json). Only copy those files plus their assets into the published location. Pros: declarative, query-driven, no temp trees/ dir. Cons: still has the transclusion-leakage problem — a published tree's HTML may have inlined content from an excluded tree, since the full build doesn't know about exclusions. So D really only works if we also enforce "published trees do not transclude unpublished trees" as a build-time check.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Chosen path: A. Option A is the only no-code option, matches upstream's actual capabilities, and unblocks publishing immediately. The directory-as-publish-gate is acknowledged as annoying — promoting a tree means physically moving it — but worth living with as a first cut. B is the natural follow-up if/when the split becomes painful; build it as a thin wrapper, not a compiler change. C and D are strictly more work for the same outcome.

Triage of trees/public/ (2026-05-29). Before turning publishing back on, the public surface was audited. Moves to private: sss-002X (TODO meeting notes), sss-002K (gardening planning), sss-001X (one-line claim, no proof), sss-002P (mid-draft stub with TODO placeholders), sss-002Q (8L stub), sss-0018 (stale Forester first-impressions). Title typos fixed in sss-002D and sss-002P (now private). Kept public on purpose: the cookbook (sss-0028 + recipes) and the halfbaked-tagged cluster (sss-002C as landing + sss-002D, sss-002E).

Dangling references fixed. Privatizing sss-001X and sss-0018 broke three public trees. sss-001N had its parenthetical link to sss-0018 removed. sss-001W and sss-0022 each had their transclusion of sss-001X replaced with a brief inline mention of the set-theoretic fact they were importing. Additionally, sss-0030 (Element of a Presheaf, a tidy Definition) was promoted from trees/ to trees/public/ — sss-002Z linked to it and it had no business being private.

Restored: public.toml (with [forest] trees = ["trees/public"] and the same url) and buildPublic.sh (which removes output/ then runs forester build public.toml -vv). ./buildPublic.sh now produces a clean output/ with no warnings.

Deployment: manual only, no schedule. The cron that drove the old flow was already removed in Forest Sync and Capture Architecture. The deploy script itself (~/stschaef.github.io/build.sh) is fine as-is — it auto-commits and auto-pushes, which is acceptable; the constraint is only that nothing invokes it on a schedule.

Hosting decision. Stay on GitHub Pages. The infrastructure (~/stschaef.github.io repo, CNAME, cleanup.sh, preserved assets like PDFs and headshot.jpeg, redirect index.html pointing at /home/) is intact. macproseph + a public-facing caddy vhost was considered but rejected — extra TLS/port-exposure work with no payoff for a hand-driven cadence.

html:p.html:strong: Manual deploy flow (what to run when publishing).

html:ul.html:li: ./build.sh — runs cleanup.sh, calls ~/forest/buildPublic.sh, removes the forester-generated output/index.html so the gh-pages redirect survives, copies output/* into the repo, stages, commits with today's date, pushes origin master, then runs ~/forest/buildPrivate.sh to restore the dev forest

fr:mainmatter.html:p: All open decisions are now resolved. The redesign captured in Website Publishing Redesign is closed by this path: option A, GitHub Pages, manual invocation. The remaining work is just to run build.sh when ready.
Rethink what gets published to stevenschaefer.net and how.

Previous setup (removed): public.toml built only trees/public/, output was copied into the GitHub Pages repo (stschaef.github.io), committed, and pushed. A crontab ran this daily at 7pm. The crontab, public.toml, and buildPublic.sh have all been removed — the redesign starts from a clean slate.

Relevant new infrastructure: macproseph now serves a static build of the full forest via caddy on the Tailscale network (see Forest Sync and Capture Architecture). The same static-build pipeline could drive public website publishing with a different forest.toml-like config applying [publish] exclusions.
Decisions needed:

html:ul.html:li: Should the website publish all non-private trees (via forest.toml with exclusion tags) or stay limited to trees/public/?
Which tags should be excluded? Candidates: private, draft, session, handwriting, agent-authored
Should publishing be triggered by the sync cron, a separate cron, or a manual command?
Should the GitHub Pages approach be kept, or move to hosting on macproseph?

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Resolved 2026-05-29. See Website publishing — paths forward without a fork for the full design and execution. Summary: stay on trees/public/ as the publish surface (no fork-style [publish] exclude_tags available upstream); GitHub Pages remains the host; deploys are manual (~/stschaef.github.io/build.sh), no cron. Publisher PDFs and private handwriting/captured assets are kept out of the public build via an asset directory split (assets/public/ vs assets/private/) plus a restricted-pdf macro defined by overlay (no-op in public, routes in dev).

Design and implement bidirectional sync for the forest between schmapple (laptop) and macproseph (home server), plus a capture endpoint for creating trees from any device.

Remove the existing crontab (0 19 * * * ~/stschaef.github.io/build.sh) which builds and deploys the public website. Website publishing is being redesigned separately (see Website Publishing Redesign).
Add a new cron/launchd job that periodically:

html:ul.html:li: Stages and commits any uncommitted changes in ~/forest
Pushes to origin (GitHub)
Pulls any new commits (e.g. trees created via the capture endpoint on macproseph)

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Serve the forest on the Tailscale network so iPad/phone can browse it.

html:ul.html:li: Clone the forest repo to /home/steven/forest
Run forester build forest.toml on a 15-minute systemd timer, producing output/
Serve output/ statically via caddy on port 8888 (Tailscale-only)
forest-pull.service commits local captures, rebases against origin, pushes, then chains into forest-build.service

fr:mainmatter.html:p: We originally planned forester serve (HTMX mode), but hit URL routing bugs — the slug link generator builds /HOST/X/ paths that don't match the server's /trees/X router. Static build sidesteps this; the XSLT link routing emits relative hrefs which work from any origin.
An HTTP endpoint on macproseph (Tailscale-only) that accepts shared content from iPad, phone, or desktop and creates a tree for it.

html:ul.html:li: Accepts POST with text, PDF, or URL
Allocates a tree ID via forester new
Writes tree content with appropriate tags (e.g. capture, handwriting for PDFs)
Commits and pushes to origin so the laptop picks it up on next sync

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Bidirectional via git through GitHub as the shared remote:

html:ul.html:li: Laptop pushes to origin on a schedule
macproseph pulls from origin on a schedule
Captures on macproseph commit + push to origin
Laptop pulls captured trees on next sync cycle

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Four signed .shortcut files in ~/forest/utils/shortcuts/, generated by gen-capture-shortcuts.py and signed with shortcuts sign --mode anyone for distribution to iPad/iPhone without the removed "Allow Untrusted Shortcuts" toggle.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: ~/nix-config/hosts/macproseph/capture-server.py, reachable at http://macproseph:8889/capture over Tailscale.

html:ul.html:li: Four payload shapes: JSON prose, JSON verbatim, JSON webclip, multipart+form, raw-body file
Every capture gets an ISO-8601 UTC \date — required for the dashboard's "most recent" pane to surface it
PDFs land as \meta{pdf}{\route-asset{...}} (theme renders a viewer); images embed via inline \<html:img>; other files link through \a

kick_sync runs in a worker thread that waits for idle then blocking-starts forest-pull.service, then re-runs if more captures arrived during the cycle — without this, a capture landing mid-build is read after the build's input pass and never makes it to output/
